set_aside.subject: R0-89 restore cutoff
set_aside.text: “That store begins its own history from the backup: every change after it is lost”
set_aside.question: After which event are changes considered lost: creation of the restored backup, loss of the live store, or some other recovery cutoff?
options: Changes after the backup was created are lost
Only changes after the live store was lost are lost
A separately recorded recovery cutoff determines the loss
set_aside.default_guess: Changes after the restored backup was created are lost.

set_aside.subject: R0-89 and request replay guarantees
set_aside.text: R0-36 says “A create repeated after a lost answer … never silently makes a second project, customer or room,” while R0-89 says guarantees hold “within each store's history” without naming R0-36 or defining a retry from the lost history.
set_aside.question: What must Registry do when a request succeeded after the restored backup was made, its answer was lost, and the same request is retried against the restored store where its replay record and created entity do not exist?
options: Treat it as a new request, allowing a duplicate across histories
Refuse it because its prior outcome cannot be established
Preserve the no-duplicate guarantee across restored histories by some external recovery mechanism
set_aside.default_guess: Treat it as a new request because R0-89 makes the restored store a new history, despite the unresolved conflict with R0-36.

set_aside.subject: R0-89 and optimistic revisions
set_aside.text: R0-35 refuses “a change against an older revision,” but R0-89 permits restoring a backup whose current record revision can be lower than the revision held by a caller from the lost history.
set_aside.question: What is the observable result when a correction presents an expected revision greater than the restored record's current revision?
options: Refuse every revision mismatch as stale or invalid
Accept because the supplied revision is not older
Return a distinct future-revision or history-mismatch failure
set_aside.default_guess: Refuse every revision mismatch and change nothing.

set_aside.subject: R0-89 audit numbering
set_aside.text: “Registry's guarantees — the log's numbering … hold within each store's history”
set_aside.question: What is numbered in the audit log, what observable invariant does that numbering guarantee, and where is the history boundary represented or exposed after a restore?
options: Entries have a sequence number that restarts or resumes from the backup within each history
Numbering is only an internal implementation detail with no external contract
Each history has an identity combined with an entry sequence number
set_aside.default_guess: Audit entries have a monotonically increasing sequence within the restored store, resuming from the last number present in the backup, with no exposed history identity.

set_aside.subject: R0-89 and erased or restricted personal data
set_aside.text: R0-89 allows a pre-change backup to replace the store and says later changes are lost, while R0-06 says erased contact values “are gone” and R0-51 says restricted data reaches no one but the owner.
set_aside.question: After restoring a backup made before an erasure or restriction, may Registry expose the restored personal data according to the older state, or must it detect and preserve the later erasure or restriction?
options: Expose according to the restored store because guarantees are per history
Refuse service until the owner reapplies post-backup privacy changes
Preserve erasures and restrictions across histories through recovery metadata
set_aside.default_guess: Expose according to the restored store because R0-89 declares post-backup changes lost, despite the unresolved conflict with the earlier absolute guarantees.
